catalogue.final:
exed**

| System | Records indexed |
|---|---|
| Shopify | 26,546 orders, 37,773 lines, 21,129 customers, 49 variants |
| Amazon | 38,264 orders, 43,513 order lines, 49 FBA inbound shipments, 25 listings (seller SKU, ASIN, FNSKU) |
| 3PL | 49 item codes, 29 receipts, 146 receipt lines, 37,331 outbound lines |
| QuickBooks | 11 vendors (vendor list only) |

- **Outbound lines:** each one points at its Shopify order or FBA shipment, and at its item.
- **Receipts:** each receipt points at the POs it covers. This created 26 empty PO records (`po/number`), which the ingestion skill will fill.

**Crosswalk.** There are 49 product hubs (our SKU). Every hub carries a Shopify variant, a 3PL item code, a UPC, a factory item code, an HS code and a supplier.
- **Exact (1.0):** UPC to Shopify variant and 3PL item code, 49 hubs. Shop SKU spelled the same as ours, 43 hubs. Amazon listing code equal to our SKU, 9 hubs.
- **Normalized (0.9):** 6 Shopify SKUs with fixed spelling (case, dropped zeros or dashes). 16 Amazon listings with `-FBA` dropped.
- **Corroborated (0.7):** factory item code, HS code and supplier for all 49, matched on the factory's invoice description equalling the shop's title plus variant. Item codes are written as `NBBW:MT-1574`.
- **Unmatched:** nothing. The 3PL's blank Client SKU rows are covered because I joined on item code and UPC.
- **Suppliers:** 8 supplier hubs, each linked to its QuickBooks vendor (0.9). The vendor's mailbox domain equals the supplier code, and its company name is printed on the supplier's invoices. The forwarder, the broker and the 3PL are QuickBooks vendors only.

**Attributes registered:** none. The installed vocabulary covered everything. I set `core/authoritative_source` on 16 identifiers (shopify, amazon, 3pl, quickbooks).

**Duplicates marked (154)**
- **Same normalized mailbox and name (0.9):** 84. The pairs I read were the same address with a plus-alias or the same address outright, with the same name and postal address.
- **Same full name and postal address (0.7):** 70. The mailboxes differ, for example `taylor.chris@` against `taylor.chris2@`. I did not read ten of these against source records.
- Nobody has more than two accounts pointing at them, and there are no chains.

**Checks**
- **Counts:** match the distinct IDs in each source.
- **Bare records:** only the 26 expected POs. No other record exists solely because a join key named it.
- **Idempotency:** a second run of the hub, supplier, FBA shipment, authority and duplicate stages wrote nothing. The Shopify and Amazon stages also came back unchanged.
- **Bug fixed:** the 3PL load had created Shopify orders by name, so the first Shopify order load collided with them. I now address orders by name.

**Left out**
- `quickbooks/transaction_list_by_vendor.csv`: general ledger, never indexed.
- WeChat chats, the ops inbox and the supplier PDFs: documents and messages for the ingestion skill. I read only the commercial invoices, for item codes, HS codes and supplier names.
- `amazon/fba_line`: the FBA export has shipment totals only, with no SKU lines.

**Terms the sources disagree on**
- **SKU:** the 3PL's Client SKU is hand-typed and has swapped letters (BKL/BLK, WTH/WHT, SVL/SLV, HFL/HLF, BMA/BAM) and blanks. Amazon appends `-FBA` for FBA stock. Shopify has six malformed spellings. The hub keeps the shop's spelling, fixed to the four-digit form. I did not store the 3PL's spelling.
- **On hand:** the 3PL's On Hand includes allocated units, and Available is on hand minus allocated, which equals Shopify's inventory quantity. Damaged is a separate column. None of this is stored.

**For you to decide**
- Whether to keep the 70 name-and-address matches at 0.7. Some may be two people at one address, such as a parent and child with the same name.
- Whether to add a receipt-to-shipment link by container number. The vocabulary has none, and the shipments don't exist until ingestion runs.
- The load script is `catalogue.py` in the work directory.

29 receipt emails.
  - Harborline Customs Brokerage: 30 entry summaries.
- Nothing was skipped as already read.

**Entities in the store**

| Kind | Count |
|---|---|
| Purchase orders (22 new) | 48 |
| PO lines | 196 |
| Shipments (32 bookings, 31 with a house bill) | 32 |
| Shipment lines | 166 |
| Inspections | 46 |
| Customs entries | 30 |
| Suppliers updated | 8 |

- **PO status:** 37 received, 4 shipped, 5 in production, 1 ready, 1 confirmed.
- **Shipments:** 29 delivered, one arrived (PBLHB2600030), one departed (PBLHB2600031) and one only booked (PBLXMN2609032).
- **House bills (HBLs) matched to bookings:** I matched on vessel, voyage and the POs on each booking. All 31 matched without ambiguity. No shipment was created twice.
- **Shared containers:** where one container carried several suppliers' POs (for example TCLU6622680), it is one shipment with lines for each PO.

**Facts written below confidence 1**
- **In production (42 facts, 0.9):** the supplier acknowledged a deposit, but their message doesn't name the PO. I linked it to the deposit message before it, matching the PO by name or by the amount against the proforma total.
- **PO ETD changes from chat (18 facts, 0.9):** these are the delays suppliers gave without a year. I took the next occurrence of the date after the message, in China time. Four of them name the proforma number instead of the PO (for example "HT-PI-2025-001"), and I mapped those through the proforma.
- **Container numbers from chat (7 facts, 0.9):** the "container loaded" messages name no PO, so I put each number on the shipment of that supplier's PO. All 7 later matched the pre-alert.

**Choices you may want to check**
- **Hash input:** for chat messages and emails I hashed the lines including their final newline, without the blank separator line. Say if you want a different convention.
- **PO status "sent":** the skill gives no trigger for it, so I never wrote it. A PO goes from nothing to confirmed at its proforma.
- **PO status "ready":** I took it only from a passed inspection report, never from a supplier saying "Goods ready". Where an inspection failed and was redone, the later passing report counts.
- **Sailing date:** when a PO became shipped, I set its ETD to the actual departure date from the pre-alert.
- **Consistency checks:** none of these disagreed with each other:
  - the chat ETDs sent with each proforma against the printed ETD;
  - invoice quantities and cartons against the pre-alerts;
  - HS codes against the SKUs;
  - customs duty plus fees against each entry's stated total.

**Unresolved**
- **PBLXMN2609032:** a booking for PO-2026-0023 with no pre-alert yet. It was rolled to ETD 6 Oct 2026 and stays "booked". The PO's ETD from chat is 1 Oct, so it is out of step with the booking and will need a new date when the supplier gives one.
- **PO-2026-0029:** its proforma is read but there is no deposit acknowledgement yet, so it stays "confirmed".

**Gaps in the vocabulary (left in the documents)**
- **Price changes (chat):**
  - Hetai: −2% from 1 July;
  - Mingjia: +3% from 1 March;
  - Qisheng: +4% from 1 May;
  - Lanxin: +5% from 15 August.
- **Holiday closures:** Chinese New Year (9 Feb to 1 Mar 2026) and National Day (1 to 7 Oct 2026).
- **Payments:** every deposit and balance, with amounts, and the "goods ready, pay balance" requests.
- **Sample couriers:** DHL air waybill numbers.
- **Warehouse receipts:** the expected, received and damaged counts per item. Examples: 24 units short on ACMH-10259 in GSF-RCV-000003, 24 short on ACMH-10294 in a February receipt, and many small damaged counts.
- **Inspection defect lists.**
- **Broker brokerage invoices:** USD 160 to 385 per entry.
- **Chat requests:** the quote requests for a new colour, and the sample requests.

The working scripts and extracted text are in the session scratchpad if you want to re-run any of it. Re-running is safe because every write goes through the lookups and nothing changes if the values are the same.

**Sources indexed.** Every ID in these sources is already in the store, checked ID by ID, so nothing is missing or extra.

| System | Record | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Shopify | orders | 26,546 |
| Shopify | line items | 37,773 |
| Shopify | customers | 21,129 |
| Shopify | variants | 49 |
| Amazon | orders | 38,264 |
| Amazon | order lines | 43,513 |
| Amazon | FBA inbound shipments | 49 |
| Amazon | ASIN, FNSKU and seller SKU | 25 products |
| 3PL | outbound lines | 37,331 |
| 3PL | receipts | 29 |

- **Hubs:** 49 SKU hubs, each carrying its Shopify variant ID, 3PL item code, UPC, supplier and HS code.
- **Amazon crosswalk:** 25 of the hubs have an Amazon ID. The other 24 aren't in the Amazon inventory file, so they look unlisted there. I didn't dig further.
- **Attributes registered:** none. The existing vocabulary covered everything.

**Not indexed**
- **Supplier PDFs, WeChat chats and the ops mbox:** these hold purchase orders, shipments and inspections, which belong to the ingestion skill, and the store already has them.
- **QuickBooks transaction list:** it is general-ledger data.
- **`fba_inventory.txt` and `inventory_snapshot.csv`:** they only repeat IDs already indexed and add quantities, which stay in the source.

**Step 7 checks**
- **Bare records:** none. Every record a join key points at is a real, complete one.
- **Duplicates:** the store held 154 `core/same_as` marks. By rule, 84 matched on a normalized mailbox and 63 on the same name and address. Seven matched neither rule, so I retracted them in transaction 207445.
  - Each of the seven pairs shared a name, but the mailboxes differ and so do the addresses. An example is `chris_m800@example.net` and `chris_m800@mail.example`.
  - The remaining 147 pairs all satisfy a rule. No account has more than three others pointing at it.

**Terms the sources disagree on:** none new. The earlier ones stay recorded as separate attributes, such as the Amazon seller SKU and the 3PL item code.

**For a human to decide**
- Do those seven pairs deserve a match after all? They have the same name but nothing else to confirm it, so I left them as separate accounts.
- No records have disappeared from a source, and no excised person has reappeared.
